extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, policymakers, and informed citizens interested in public opinion, democratic procedure, and civic education
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance and practical standards for when and how public opinion should be invoked, how representative institutions and expert intelligence should mediate complex issues, and how civic education and reason can be cultivated to improve democratic decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation of federalism in shared ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Federalism swings toward centralization or anarchy unless the union is based on correct and commonly accepted ideas of federal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ideas "do not arise spontaneously" but must be pieced together by generalization based on analysis; instruments for that analysis must be invented and tested by research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforms must overcome subjectivism of individual experience
rubrics_metrics.description: No electoral device or manipulation substitutes for overcoming the subjectivism of human opinion grounded in limited individual experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reform is not truly radical unless it consciously provides a way of overcoming subjective opinion by promoting knowledge drawn from the environment rather than inner conscience or prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence bureaus should serve men of action
rubrics_metrics.description: An intelligence system's primary value is as an instrument for representatives, administrators, and workers doing public business, not to burden every citizen with expert opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its real use is to aid representative government and administration; secondarily it is a source of general information and a check on the daily press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift burden of technical judgment to responsible administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume every citizen can digest expert reports; push the burden of technical judgment away from the general public toward those charged with decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized actors (committeemen, officers, union officials, industrial councils) and voluntary societies with staffs should study documents and make reports that serve as checks on officialdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public scrutiny should focus on procedure and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsiders can legitimately judge whether relevant facts were considered, whether interested groups were heard, whether ballots were honest, and whether results were honestly accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public can watch procedure when news indicates something to watch; substantive technical relevance is for experts to decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bringing every intricate matter directly to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Appealing to the public on intricate matters often aims to escape expert criticism by enlisting an uninformed majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such appeals make verdicts depend on who has the loudest voice or best publicity, and the public is typically not equipped to substitute for procedures designed to handle complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insist issues pass through proper procedure before public appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems should not be brought to the general public until they have passed through a procedure that tests and clarifies the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative bodies should ensure issues are analyzed by experts and debated in the presence of mediators who force discussion to deal with expert analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use neutral chairmen/mediators to force fact-based dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Partisan voices belong at the table but must be confronted by neutral men who control the facts and have the dialectical skill to separate real perception from stereotype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Socratic-like mediation requires figures who have explored the environment as well as the human mind, and who can summon consulting experts to substitute data for slogans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on transparent evidence and official data when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace vague partisan assertions (e.g., 'well paid' vs 'exploited') with concrete data such as wage tables, budgets, and price statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private books or claims are withheld, a chairman should note the refusal and issue public statements based on official figures, and refer disputes about data to standing intelligence committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert mediation aims to disintegrate partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of expert mediation is not coercion but the breaking up of partisan stereotyping so outsiders avoid being entangled by slogans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if partisans remain unconvinced, others are enabled to form less entangled, more objective judgments after mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise naming and definition to disentangle emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Turning abstract charged words (e.g., 'Labor is Exploited') into specific, named claims (e.g., 'groups C and M are underpaid') objectifies ideas and makes the emotion they arouse specific and corrigible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once ideas are defined and externalized, they are open to correction by new data and criticism; naming separates 'me' from 'that' and reduces defensive resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critics need valid empirical pictures from expert reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic dialectic by critics is limited unless they can count on expert reporters to furnish a valid picture of the environment relevant to the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intelligence work is required for political and industrial problems; without accurate information, critical methods can't progress far.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic gathering of social knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of social information must become the normal accompaniment of action, turning accumulated data into generalizations usable by political science and schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As data accumulates, civic education and conceptual pictures of the world can be developed, enabling preparation for unseen environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic education should train habits of source-scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should prepare pupils to examine sources: dispatch origin, correspondent names, press service, authority for statements, and conditions of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the case method, history, comparative history, and anthropology to instill habits of introspection about imagery, awareness of censorship and propaganda, and recognition of stereotypes, allegories, dramatization, and personification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach identification of cognitive errors and introspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should make pupils aware of how their minds construct allegories, dramatize relations, personify abstractions, and adopt heroic/romantic/economic attitudes when holding opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize study of error as prophylactic and as an engaging introduction to scientific method; teach students to detach ideas from self-identity to allow correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to reason requires long-run stability and time
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasoning on political matters is practicable mainly where there is some stability over long durations; immediate crises often preclude constructive appeals to reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reason evolves slowly and political action often requires quick responses, cultivate institutions and habits that allow longer time-horizons to influence decisions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for time horizons when assessing plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevancy and practicability of any plan depend on the length of time required and whether its assumed data will remain stable during that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political philosophers should study the element of time in politics; realistic actors intuitively estimate rates of social change when distinguishing opportunists, visionaries, and experienced men.

rubrics_metrics.name: In crises use available quick means while cultivating reason
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergencies there may be no time to educate or to make everyone an expert; immediate means (speech, slogans, force, compromise) may be necessary, though not ideal for reasoned solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to emergency measures, use wit and force to create footholds for reason and try to lengthen the time perspective where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral standards in the appeal to reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Hatred, intolerance, suspicion, bigotry, secrecy, fear, and lying have no place in appeals to reason and are poisons to public opinion in the long run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate decency, good will, and an ingrained prejudice against these vices; maintain faith in the possibility of better human conduct despite historical brutality.
